With the wolf player_1 finally gone, we are in a strong position to clear the remaining threat. player_2, looking back at the voting history, you were very persistent in opposing the investigator early on, which makes me wonder where your loyalties truly lie.

It is true that I was skeptical, but that was because I genuinely doubted the investigator's claims at the time—many of us did, especially given how chaotic those days were. I've been focused on weeding out threats to the village this whole time. Now that player_1 is confirmed as a wolf, we need to shift our attention to the serial killer who has been making moves behind the scenes. Does anyone have a theory on who that might be?

It is true that the investigator's claims were volatile, but now that we have confirmation about player_1, we really need to look at who stood to benefit from the confusion. player_8, you were quick to jump on the bandwagon against player_9 yesterday. Is there a reason you are so certain about player_2 now instead of looking at the pattern of who was consistently shielding player_1 during the earlier ties?

My vote against player_9 was based on their relentless push to eliminate people based on the investigator's old claims, which I thought was distracting us. I was questioning player_2 because their history with player_1 was so closely aligned during those tie votes. I'm just trying to make sense of the patterns we've seen so we don't pick the wrong person now.

It's understandable to look at voting history, but I think focusing solely on past tie votes ignores the fact that we were all operating under incomplete information. If I were a wolf, I wouldn't have been as vocal about questioning the investigator's methods when it was making me a target. At this point, we need to consider who has consistently survived while avoiding the heat, as the serial killer has been avoiding detection by letting us eliminate each other.

player_8, questioning the alignment between player_1 and player_2 makes sense, but you were just as consistent in that bloc during the early ties. Why should we view your past voting as objective analysis rather than a cover for your own survival while the wolves were active?

My votes were consistently aimed at testing the reliability of the investigator's claims when they were disrupting the town, player_7. I wasn't shielding player_1; I was challenging a volatile situation. If we're looking at patterns of survival, we should look at who stayed out of the line of fire while the rest of us were debating the investigator's claims. Why should I be considered more suspicious than you for trying to clear the board of distractions?

We need to stop rehashing the early days when we were all guessing. The reality is that player 1 was a wolf, and the investigator was right about them. The problem now is the serial killer. If we keep fighting each other over past voting blocs that were formed when nobody knew anyone's true role, the serial killer just wins by default. We should look at who has been the most aggressive in steering the current conversation to keep us deadlocked.

player_8, you claim your votes were to test the investigator, yet you were part of the same bloc that resisted them. If we are looking for the serial killer, they thrive on this circular logic about past voting. Let's look at the night actions: the serial killer has been active throughout. Between the two of you, who has the most consistent theory on the remaining wolf versus the serial killer?

With player 1 out, we have a grim start. Since no one has made any bold claims or suspicious moves yet, I think it's safest to keep our eyes open during today's vote. Let's see who jumps to defend or accuse whom once we actually start putting names forward.

Player 3 is right, we have almost no information to go on yet. Voting blindly now is just helping the wolves or the serial killer. Maybe we should look at who seems to be trying to control the narrative or force a vote too early later on.
I agree with player 3 and 9. Trying to force a vote now without any leads is just gambling, and I'd rather wait until we have a bit more to discuss before throwing around accusations.

It is tough losing the healer so early. We need to be careful now since we have no protection left. I still don't see any clear patterns, so maybe we should just focus on who was most active yesterday to see if anyone is pushing too hard for a specific target.

Losing the healer is a huge blow. With no protection, we are all exposed, so we should focus on the most logical candidates based on the remaining voting history. We've been abstaining too much, which only helps the scum hide. If we continue this way, we'll just run out of time.

I agree with player_9 that the repeated abstentions are working against us. We're effectively giving the killers a free pass to operate in the shadows. We should start voting based on who is trying to lead the conversation too aggressively now that the board is thinning out.

We have two nights of kills and zero votes against anyone. I agree that we cannot keep abstaining. If we don't start voting, we're just waiting to be picked off. Does anyone have a specific player they think acted suspiciously during the last few discussions?

We need to stop spinning our wheels. Since player_3 is a villager, we can at least count them as a secure vote for the village. Let's look at who was most eager to push for an 'abstain' in previous rounds, as that passive behavior clearly benefited the wolves and the SK.

I agree that we need to stop abstaining, but we have to be careful. Since we don't have clear leads yet, blindly voting might just eliminate a fellow villager. Let's look at the past discussions to see if anyone's defensive posture changed when the pressure started to mount.

We need to stop guessing and start tracking. If we can't find clear leads on behaviors, we should pick someone to investigate or challenge their claims directly to force a reaction. Let's look at player_4 and player_8; they have been quiet compared to others, maybe we should ask them for their current thoughts on who is most suspicious?

Player 9, you mentioned looking at player 4 and 8. I think that's a good start, but we should also analyze why player 6 is suggesting we look at 'active' players now, when they were part of the group pushing for abstentions earlier. Has your read on the risk changed, player 6?

That's a fair question, player 3. My earlier support for abstaining was because we genuinely had zero information to go on, and I didn't want to risk an innocent player on a hunch. Now that the healer is dead and we've had more time to observe, it's clear the status quo isn't working. My shift in thinking is simply a response to the fact that we're losing ground, not a change in my intentions.

Player 6, I understand the desire for caution, but we've wasted two days abstaining while we lose our power roles. If we are now forced to act because of the healer's death, why not propose a concrete test? Everyone seems to agree we need to stop the cycle of abstaining, so let's put it to the test and see who resists the first real vote.

I've been quiet because I haven't seen anything concrete enough to justify a shot or a firm accusation yet. We were all being cautious by abstaining, but the loss of the healer changes the math. Player 9, I hear you, but why look at 4 and me specifically instead of looking at the people who consistently pushed for the abstain policy during the last two days?

I agree with player 8 that we shouldn't just look at who was quiet. I asked about you and player 4 because you hadn't weighed in yet, and in a game where information is scarce, silence is the only thing we can measure. If we want to break the cycle, we need someone to propose a target based on those previous abstain records instead of just debating the policy itself. Who exactly are you suggesting we start with, player 8?

Player 8, you make a fair point. Looking at the history, those who were most vocally pushing for abstention during days 1 and 2—like player 6 or even myself—bear the most responsibility for our current lack of information. Since we need to test the room, I am open to looking at the voting records of those who were most eager to delay. Does anyone have a specific player from that group they feel is still hiding behind caution?

I agree that we need to stop circling the issue. If we are looking at the voting records, let's examine the consistency of those who advocated for abstention versus those who were just following the consensus. Since we are all now acknowledging that the previous strategy failed, the real test is who is willing to commit to a specific vote today, rather than just theorizing about who was responsible. I am willing to vote today to break this deadlock, so let's pick a candidate who has been avoiding any firm stance.

We have spent too much time discussing the concept of voting instead of actually voting. Since player_3 is a confirmed villager, I propose we look at the players who are now suddenly demanding action after being the loudest proponents of abstaining. It is easy to pivot to 'pro-action' when you realize you're under suspicion. Let's start by pressure-testing those who reversed their stance most dramatically today.

I agree that we need to stop just talking about the concept of voting and actually commit to one. I am not trying to pivot just to avoid suspicion; I am trying to correct our previous collective mistake. Since I am willing to vote today, let's put that to the test. Who are you proposing we look at, player 7, and why them specifically?

Player 9, you keep asking for a target, but demanding a target without evidence is just as risky as the constant abstaining we did before. Player 7, calling out people for 'pivoting' is fair, but everyone here has essentially done that. If we are going to break the deadlock, I'm willing to vote today, but we need to stop debating the history and start looking at who is actually willing to cast the first real vote when the time comes.

Player 7, you're right that pivoting is suspicious, but calling for action is the only way to get anywhere now. If everyone keeps waiting for the 'perfect' evidence, we'll lose another villager tonight. Let's quit the circular talk—I'm ready to vote for someone who consistently pushed for abstention if they can't provide a real candidate now. Player 6, since you're the one saying you're ready to break the deadlock, put a name on the table.

I hear you, player 3. It feels like we are all in a high-stakes standoff. If I suggest someone and it looks like a deflection, I end up on the chopping block; if I don't, I look like I'm still stalling. I'm willing to support a vote on whoever shows the most hesitation when we finally move to the formal vote, but I won't be the one to single-handedly point a finger on a guess. Let's see who among us actually commits to a name first.

We are talking in circles. Player 6, you say you are ready to break the deadlock but refuse to name a target because you fear being the one to point fingers. That hesitation is exactly what the wolves need. If we don't start naming names now, we're just waiting for the next night kill. Since you all want to see who commits, I'm willing to start by looking at player 9, who has been aggressively pushing for others to lead while avoiding naming a concrete target themselves. Let's see if that sparks a real vote.

Player 4, accusing me of avoiding a target because I'm pushing for others to lead is a bit rich. I've been calling for a vote precisely because I'm tired of the inaction, and my focus on you and player 8 was an attempt to find out who was genuinely contributing versus just observing. If my call for action is 'aggressive,' then what do you call the total vacuum of leads we've had for two days? I'm ready to commit to a vote, but I'd rather see a logical candidate emerge from our past records than just picking a random person to appease the fear of the room.

Being the Investigator, I suspect they hit me because I might be a threat to their plans, but since I am a villager, it just shows they are trying to eliminate anyone who might expose them. original.text: We are down to the final three, and every vote now is essentially game-ending. Looking at our history, player 5 and player 9 both participated in the push against the investigator, which remains the most pivotal error we've made. We need to be absolutely certain before casting a vote today, because if we misfire here, the game is over for whoever is left. I'm hesitant to make a move without considering if one of you is trying to bait me into the final error.

day_channel.message: Since it is the first day and we have no information, perhaps we should suggest everyone reveal who they think is the most suspicious once we actually have some data. For now, there isn't much to go on, so let's keep an eye on how everyone votes later.

Player 1, I agree that jumping to conclusions without any data is dangerous. Since we're all flying blind today, maybe we should focus on establishing a baseline for how we share information once we have it, rather than just waiting to vote.

I agree with player_9. We don't have enough to go on right now to start pointing fingers, but we should definitely set a precedent for transparency. Once we have at least one or two rounds of voting, we will have actual records to analyze instead of just gut feelings.

Here's the vote result for day 1:

No vote was held today; no one is eliminated.
Night of day 1: player_1 was attacked by the serial killer but was saved by the healer!

It's good that player_1 survived the night. Since the healer has shown their hand, we need to be very careful about who we target today. Does anyone have thoughts on why someone would go after player_1 immediately, or does that seem like a random kill?

It feels like a random shot to me, player_7. If they were looking for a high-value target, they might have gone for someone more vocal yesterday. Honestly, the killer could just be trying to fish for information on who the healer is, which is a dangerous game for the village.

It is hard to read intent behind a first-night attack. Sometimes players strike early to see how the room reacts, or they might just be guessing blindly. With no vote yet, we are still waiting for actual behavior to analyze.

The attack on player_1 was definitely targeted, not random. Since the healer revealed their protection, we need to protect player_1 today while we look for patterns in the upcoming vote. Does anyone have a theory on who might have benefit from outing the healer this early?

Actually, I disagree with the idea that the attack was random or just fishing for the healer. It was a very specific choice. If we really want to progress, we should focus on player 1. I've been looking at their contributions, and something feels off. I think we should consider them for elimination today.

I'm genuinely surprised by that stance, player_9. We agreed that information was scarce, and now you want to eliminate someone solely based on a 'gut feeling' after I was targeted for a night kill? Pushing for a vote on someone who was already the victim of a night attack feels like an attempt to capitalize on the chaos rather than actually hunting for wolves.

It isn't about capitalizing on chaos, player_1. I simply think your behavior doesn't align with someone genuinely trying to help the village find the actual threats. Sometimes a gut feeling is just the recognition of patterns that don't add up, and I believe looking into your role is the most logical step for us right now.

Calling a gut feeling 'logical' is a reach, player 9. We have zero voting records and no night-kill patterns, yet you're targeting someone who was already the recipient of an attack. If the goal is truly finding wolves, why start by pushing for an elimination on someone who's already been vetted by the healer's protection? It feels like you're trying to force a lynch to hide your own intentions rather than looking for actual clues.

My skepticism isn't based on being 'vetted' by a healer, but on how you maneuver through these discussions to avoid real scrutiny. Being attacked at night doesn't make you a villager, it just means the killer had a reason to target you. I am not trying to hide my intentions; I am trying to eliminate a player who is actively deflecting away from meaningful analysis.

It seems premature to jump on player_1 just because they were targeted at night. Being attacked isn't evidence of guilt, and rushing an elimination this early based on a 'gut feeling' feels more like a distraction than a solution. Why is player_9 so convinced of their guilt without a single vote cast yet?

Player 4, it isn't about being 'convinced' of guilt without evidence; it's about identifying patterns in how a player controls the conversation. While being attacked at night is not proof of guilt, I've observed consistent deflection from player 1 that doesn't serve the village's need for transparency. I am advocating for this vote because we need to start somewhere, and I would rather prioritize removing someone whose communication style is consistently evasive than wait for a 'perfect' piece of evidence that may never come.

player_9, you are pushing for an elimination based solely on a gut feeling while admitting there is no hard evidence. Attacking someone just because they were the target of a night kill—which we now know was blocked by the healer—is an odd move that feels more like you're trying to finish a job the killer started. If player_1 is suspicious, what specific logic or contradiction are you seeing beyond just their 'tone'?

Player 7, I understand why my push seems abrupt. My logic isn't just about the night attack; it's about observing how player 1 steers the conversation away from accountability whenever they are questioned. We are in a game where we have to make tough calls early, and I believe my read on their deflection patterns is the most actionable lead we have. I am not trying to 'finish a job,' I am trying to remove someone who is actively muddying the waters.

I find player_9's intensity concerning. Pushing for an immediate elimination on someone who was clearly targeted by the serial killer feels like a strategic move to clear the board rather than a logical deduction. Let's not rush into a vote that could remove a player without more concrete evidence than 'gut feelings.'

Player 8, I understand the optics. It looks like I am picking on the person who was already targeted. However, I have information that makes this far more than just a gut feeling. I have been investigating, and I am confident that player 1 is a threat to this village. We cannot afford to wait for 'perfect evidence' when we have a confirmed wolf in our midst. My intensity comes from knowing the reality of the situation, and I am prepared to be the one to push for this necessary elimination.

player_9, you just claimed to have information that makes this 'more than a gut feeling.' Are you claiming to be the investigator, or do you have some other source of info? If you are the investigator, you should be very careful about outing yourself before we have a consensus, as the wolves will target you tonight.

Player 3, you are right to be cautious, but I cannot sit on this information while a wolf openly manipulates the group. I am indeed the investigator, and I investigated player 1 last night. The result is definitive. We have a clear path to neutralize a wolf, and I am willing to bear the risk to my own safety if it means removing a confirmed threat from this game.

Player 9, claiming the investigator role this early is a massive move. If you're right, we have a lead, but if you're wrong, you've just handed the wolves a high-value target for tonight. I'm going to watch the voting record carefully on this one. If 1 is eliminated, we better see a reveal that confirms your claim, or you'll be the one under the microscope tomorrow.

Player 9, this is a very convenient role claim to save your argument after you realized it was falling apart. If you were the real investigator, you would know that claiming this early just makes you the primary target for the wolves tonight, which is exactly what a wolf would do to create chaos or trade lives. It is much more likely that you are either the serial killer trying to eliminate a player who survived their attack, or a wolf trying to clear the board. Does anyone else see how convenient it is that they only 'found' this information exactly when they were being questioned for their aggressive behavior?

Player 9, claiming the investigator role only after being cornered is extremely suspicious. If you are the investigator, you have just put the largest target on your back and forced our hand. If player 1 flips anything other than a wolf, we know exactly who the next target should be. I'm wary of this being a desperate play to secure an elimination.

Player 4, I understand the optics are challenging, but I am prioritizing the survival of the village over my own longevity. I did not 'wait' to claim; I shared the information precisely when the pushback against my logic made it clear that we were at a standstill. If I am wrong, the village has every right to vote me out next. But if I am right, we lose a wolf today. I ask that you look at the risk-reward: I am putting myself on the line to confirm a threat that is already here.

player_9, making an investigator claim under pressure is a massive gamble that fundamentally shifts the game. If you are telling the truth, you have essentially traded your life for a wolf's. We need to be absolutely certain before we commit to this. Player_1, what is your defense to this specific claim? Everyone else, we should observe who is eager to follow player_9's lead versus who is hesitant, as that might reveal the wolf pack's voting patterns.

Player 7, my defense is simple: the timing is everything. Look at the progression—player 9 started by attacking me purely on 'gut feelings,' was pushed for evidence, and then suddenly produced a 'result' as an investigator the moment their survival became uncertain. This is the definition of a desperate, last-ditch effort to manufacture a lynch. If they were truly the investigator, they would have let us build our own logic instead of trying to steamroll a vote based on a role claim that cannot be proven until I am gone. By rushing this, they are forcing the village to gamble on their word alone, which is a perfect cover for a wolf to eliminate an innocent player.

The village chose to abstain. No one is eliminated today.
Night of day 2: player_9 was attacked by the wolves and the serial killer last night. They were a investigator.

It's tough losing the investigator, even if player_9's claim was controversial. Since we're still without a clear lead, we need to focus on who pushed for the abstention last round and why. Let's see if anyone's voting behavior changes today.
